name: Should drywall repairs be finished before painting starts in a foreclosed home?

mainEntity.name: Should drywall repairs be finished before painting starts in a foreclosed home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Drywall repair should always be completed before applying primer or finish paint in a foreclosed home. Foreclosures routinely feature settlement cracks, door handle punctures, missing sections from utility work, or water-damaged ceilings. Painting damaged drywall first results in uneven texture, visible seams, and wasted materials. At HH Remodeling, our crew handles custom drywall patching, taping, mudding, and texture matching directly on-site. Once the drywall patches are cured, sanded flush, and sealed, the painting process proceeds uniformly, ensuring an even sheen and durable finish across the entire room.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. All drywall patching, mudding, and texture matching must be completely finished and cured before painting to ensure an even, professional finish.
